draft.title: Poetic forms
card: a short poem of three lines, traditionally 5, 7 and 5 syllables. The tiny space suits a single image or moment.
a five-line poem with a bouncing rhythm and an AABBA rhyme pattern. The rhyme and rhythm suit a funny story.
a poem that tells a story, often in four-line stanzas with rhyme and a steady beat. It suits a tale that is easy to follow and remember.
a poem with no set rhyme, rhythm or line length. The poet decides where each line ends, so the shape can follow the idea.
draft.remember: A poem's form sets rules for lines, syllables or rhyme, and those rules shape what the poem can do.

a.q: Which form has three short lines of 5, 7 and 5 syllables?
a.why: A haiku is a three-line poem with 5, 7 and 5 syllables. A limerick has five lines and an AABBA rhyme pattern, so it does not fit.
a.clue: Count the lines first: the form has only three.

b.q: Sam wants to write a poem about a school sports day. He wants it to be funny, with a bouncing rhythm and rhymes at the line ends. Which form suits his aim best?
b.why: A limerick has a bouncing rhythm and an AABBA rhyme, which suits a funny story. A ballad also uses rhyme, but it is a story poem in four-line stanzas and is not set up for a quick joke.
b.clue: Which form is built on rhyme and rhythm for a joke?
